target_customer: US warehouse and distribution operators that move cases by hand and have not automated
problem: Most US warehouses have no automation because existing robotics cost too much and are hard to integrate, so labor stays the main cost. Manifold sells robot labor priced per pick with no upfront cost.
business_model: robotics as a service, usage-based pricing per pick
product_category: warehouse robotics (case picking, truck loading and unloading, palletizing)

founders.name: Nicolas Yeh
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page, grew up in a third-generation family supply chain business supplying consumer products to US retailers.

founders.name: Joshua Ibrahim
education: MS and BS Electrical and Systems Engineering, University of Pennsylvania
founders.background_notes: Research focus on safety-critical control for robotics, per the YC page.

competitors.name: Lumper
competitors.what: Autonomous warehouse robots sold by the pick with no upfront cost, starting with palletizing
competitors.traction_then: not stated in the source; vendor claims only

competitors.name: Locus Robotics (Locus Array)
competitors.what: Mobile base with vision and arm for autonomous fulfillment picking, sold as a system

competitors.name: Brightpick (Gridpicker)
competitors.what: Robotic fulfillment system for high throughput picking

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable case picking, unloading and palletizing across varied boxes needs a 6-DOF arm, suction gripper, vision, LiDAR mobile base and remote operator fallback. A two person team must integrate hardware and software with ERP, WMS and WES systems.

defensibility.rationale: Pay per pick pricing is a financing model that others such as Lumper already offer. Deployed data and integrations could create some lock-in, but nothing structural is shown yet.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to know. Funded rivals launched case picking and per pick offerings in 2026.

market_need_then: The company cites $75bn of annual US warehouse labor spend and only 10 percent of warehouses with any automation, which are its own figures from the YC page.

identity.logo: not described by any source seen
identity.visual_style: clean, minimal layout with numbered steps and a book a deployment call button
identity.voice_and_tone: short, direct, benefit focused claims such as Priced by the pick

brand_strength.rationale: Only a company site and YC page exist. A job board profile flagged brand confusion with other Manifold companies, such as Manifold Freight and Manifold Robotics, but that is a third party view.

outcome_analysis: Manifold is a two person Summer 2026 company that has just launched, so there is no outcome yet. It pairs a technical founder with robotics control research and a supply chain operator, and sells robot labor per pick to remove upfront cost. The main risks are hardware execution and well funded warehouse robotics rivals that launched case picking in 2026.
notes: Dealroom lists a 125k dollar seed round with no date or investors and I found no second source, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. The company site lists YC and Timeless as partners, no amounts. Competitor items were found through vendor and trade press with approximate dates. The YC page company description says Los Angeles, team of 2.
